rule: 2.3 may turn only a detector TRUSTED by the 2.2 protocol (today: corrections) into suggestions; every other detector's output stays report-only until a re-run of that protocol on a fresh held-out corpus trusts it.
chose: 2.2 VERDICTS under the pre-registered protocol (detect @ b219616, labels frozen at eval git 3abbf41, results 9fed5a9, results.json sha256 167bae8ac4ccf109; held-out = validation ∪ operator):
- corrections — TRUSTED: 28 TP / 1 FP, precision 0.97 [Wilson 0.83, 0.99]; recall 0.53 (25 of 53 record fixes left no correction event — re-logged decisions, re-sent plans); 26 of the 28 TP come from the operator split.
- duplicate_session_starts — UNTRUSTED, insufficient evidence (1 judged finding); recall 3/31. - formatter_friction — UNTRUSTED: 2 TP / 1 FP, and coverage violations on 5 units (it printed 0 where losses exist: Codex never fires the hooks, and calib-1 edited biome.json before any initiative existed).

Regression rediscovery: 3 of 4 preview rows found (smoke-1 duplicate starts, smoke-2 corrections, smoke-4 codex-drive stall); calib-1's biome edit was missed.
over: Reporting the smoke rediscovery as validation; trusting duplicate_session_starts on its 1.00 precision point estimate (n=1); treating formatter_friction's zeros on Codex cells as "no friction".
because: The gate was fixed before labels existed and is applied as written. Precision gates what reaches a suggestion, but the recall numbers change what the detectors may be used FOR: r1-fixes 1.2 predicts "0 duplicate session_started in round-2 cursor cells", and a detector that sees 10% of re-registrations cannot measure that prediction. The zero-prints are the audit's S1 failure (a count for an unobserved signal) reproduced on real logs. The availability map degrades against the clone's settings and store path only, never against whether the CORPUS contains the signal's source.
